Writes resolve successfully inside the sandbox but never persist." That is the only isolation stated for an environment that runs untrusted page JavaScript on Tessel infrastructure. There is no network egress restriction, no block on private, internal or metadata addresses, and no statement that it holds no credentials. blocking: [opus-for-opus2] C/project/docs/metadata.md:56 runs author JavaScript for every public or unlisted page lacking a static title or description ("The job loads the content URL in a headless browser") with no network sandboxing. The only stated isolation is preview-mode writes. Page code can reach internal services or cloud metadata endpoints from Tessel's job workers (SSRF), and can perform side effects against third-party APIs on every publish.

[opus-for-opus2] C/project/docs/metadata.md:14 puts author HTML on a separate content origin that, by design, never holds Tessel session cookies. The doc never says how that origin authorizes a private page's HTML, and :114 "Re-hosted assets for a private page are served only to members" has no mechanism on a cookieless origin. A preview tool given the iframe's content URL (or anyone holding it) would get the private page's own <title> and text, which reopens bug 233 on that surface. A, by contrast, specifies a short-lived signed token.

[opus-for-opus2] C/project/docs/metadata.md:122 places the write gate inside the runtime in the page's own realm ("the runtime refuses writes until the page has received a trusted user interaction"). :124 concedes "The write gate protects against well-behaved automation, not attackers." Page code shares the realm and can bypass it, and the server enforces nothing.
